hypotheses.reasoning: The login 503s originate in account-svc's AuthClient calling auth-svc POST /tokens. Auth-svc began a rolling deploy of v4.3.0 at 11:08:57 (#3094); instance auth-svc-1 drained at 11:09:02, dropping capacity to 3/4 (#3114), and returned to 4/4 only at 11:09:40 (#3212). Shortly after the first 503 from auth-svc (#3197), account-svc retries immediately with backoff disabled (#3197, #3500, #3612; retry delay 0ms at #3371). Auth-svc then saw inbound rate 3.2x baseline with 732 inflight (#3364), load-shed with queue-full 503s (#3347 and later), and admission control rejected work (#3590). Edge-proxy then returned POST /login 503s after retries were exhausted (#3501, #3271). The retry amplification keeps auth-svc saturated, which explains 'not recovering' even after the rollout finished. The trigger is small (one instance drained during a rollout); the damage is amplification.

The auth-svc v4.3.0 rollout at 11:08:57 is the closest change preceding onset. The rollout reduced capacity to 3/4 and the instance returned by 11:09:40, but no log line shows v4.3.0 itself erroring; the overload persisted well after the rollout finished, so the release is at most a partial trigger rather than the origin of the fault.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately enable exponential backoff with jitter and a bounded retry budget in account-svc's AuthClient so it stops hammering auth-svc; consider a circuit breaker. Temporarily reduce edge-proxy retries on /login. Scale auth-svc or raise its admission limits to drain the backlog, then verify the login 503 rate falls below threshold. Pause or roll back the auth-svc v4.3.0 rollout if capacity does not recover. Separately (not the login cause): report-cron nightly-revenue-report fails on a missing pandas module since image 2026.10.2, and event-processor is stuck on a NUL-byte poison message msg-992570 at events.raw partition 10 (#3639, #3720, #4005), causing consumer lag; these need their own tickets.
